leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as their round-1 configuration. All five name the same two laureates and cite the magic-wavelength idea, accuracy near 1e-18, and independent confirmation at JILA, RIKEN, SYRTE, PTB and NIST. The citation wordings differ slightly: some stress invention and realisation of the clock, others the 1e-18 level of precision, and Danielsson and Kroll want the instrument and its physics, not the pending redefinition of the second, to carry the case. Two members (Danielsson, Johansson) moved to this ballot after reading the other ballots, so part of the support is recent and was not a first choice for them at the opening stage. What is not shared is the answer to whether this is a discrete discovery or the crossing of a precision threshold in a field already honoured in 1997, 2005, 2012 and 2018. Every supporter also lists an unresolved credit question about Lemonde, Derevianko or other lattice-clock groups.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, and both use essentially the same citation: prediction of flat bands at a magic angle plus experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. They share the view that theory-then-experiment is the strongest structure on the shortlist and that the phenomenology has been reproduced widely and extended to other moire systems. Mehlig moved to this ballot from active-matter hydrodynamics after reading the others, so the position is partly a consolidation. B047 is also named as an alternative by Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce, so its breadth of second-choice support is notable, but each of those members raises maturity or credit concerns. The supporters accept that the pairing mechanism is unsettled and that Cao, Fatemi and other 2018 first authors are outside the names; they differ on how much that weakens the case.

One member prefers topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) and puts the case on stability of interpretation, more than fifteen years of independent confirmation, and the sequence of prediction, material route and experiment. The same member names the weak points: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal is outside the names (and Zhang has died), the 3D pioneers are uncredited, and the 2016 topological-phases prize is close. Johansson ranks it second and shares the 2016-overlap and credit-gap worries, and Mehlig, who ranked it low, raises the same two points. No other member explicitly prefers it.

areas_of_agreement: No member prefers a configuration other than B019, B047 or B012. B019 and B047 recur as alternatives across the committee, and B012 is named only by Eriksson and Olsson as a preferred choice or alternative.
Katori and Ye are named by every member who proposes B019, and no member proposes a different pair for the clock candidate. Nobody argues that the clock science is unreplicated.

Every member who engages with B047 accepts that the 2018 correlated and superconducting phases and the flat-band prediction are real and widely reproduced, and that the superconducting pairing mechanism is not settled.

Members accept that credit gaps cannot be repaired inside a three-name limit for B012 (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and B047 (Cao, Fatemi and other first authors), and that the committee should say so openly rather than stretch the citation.

Several members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth) treat the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits as a reason to hold circuit QED (B004) for a later cycle, though they rest this on committee practice and not on a physics objection.
scientific_disputes: Lattice clocks (B019): is the magic-wavelength trap with a 1e-18 systematic budget a distinct physical discovery, as Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and I argue, or a long refinement of precision spectroscopy built on the frequency comb and ion-control prizes, as Eriksson, Mehlig and Kroll's own case_against allow? Mehlig ranked it only sixth on this ground.

Twisted bilayer graphene (B047): does the prize need the superconducting mechanism to be understood (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson on timing), or does the existence of the correlated and superconducting phases at the predicted angle suffice (Mehlig, Olsson, Eriksson in response)?

Topological insulators (B012): is the Z2 quantum spin Hall state a new class of matter distinct from the 2016 prize (Eriksson), or is part of the field implicitly covered (Johansson, Mehlig raise this)?

Active matter (B009) is not a preferred configuration for any member after Mehlig's move, but Mehlig, Eriksson and Danielsson still disagree about whether the Toner-Tu and Ramaswamy exponents have been tested quantitatively enough to compare it with a result like quantised conductance.
attribution_disputes: B019: Katori and Ye are uncontested among supporters, but Lemonde (SYRTE), Derevianko (theory of magic wavelengths and shifts), the Ludlow and Hinkley teams and the single-ion clock groups are raised as possible omissions. Kroll and Lindroth would not extend the prize to theory, and Johansson and Kroll ask for a check of the priority record for the first Sr lattice clock.

B047: Bistritzer is kept by Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce as a third name for the continuum-model prediction, but the experimental side is carried by Jarillo-Herrero alone and Cao, Fatemi and other 2018 co-authors are outside the names. Olsson also asks whether parallel moire work by other groups needs a priority check.

B012: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp realised, Zhang has died, and Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele and Hasan on the 3D side are not credited. Eriksson would restrict the citation to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect.

Similar proposals differ in citation scope. For B019, wording runs from the clock as an invention to the 1e-18 accuracy to the magic-wavelength concept plus its realisation. For B047, the two supporters word the citation as prediction plus discovery, while Danielsson and Johansson speak of experimental credit being the weakest part. For B012, a narrow 2D quantum spin Hall citation and a broader topological-insulator citation lead to different laureate sets.
maturity_disputes: B019 is described as the most mature candidate by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce, who cite independent confirmation and agreed uncertainty budgets. Pearce, Danielsson and Kroll agree the pending redefinition of the second is prospective and should not carry the case.

B047 is eight years old. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson and Pearce think it may be premature while the pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder questions remain. Mehlig and Olsson reply that the discovery and its reproduction are established and waiting is not neutral.

B012 has the longest independent confirmation record (more than fifteen years across transport, ARPES and calculation), which Eriksson counts as the strongest maturity evidence, while others discount it for the 2016 overlap and the credit gap.

B004 is flagged by Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth as too close to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits. Johansson and Kroll add that the transmon, Devoret and Girvin credit questions are unresolved.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs WACQT and works in superconducting circuits, knows Wallraff, Schoelkopf and Blais and the 2025 laureates (guest researchers at Chalmers), and says he should recuse or discount his view on B004.
Kroll is on the WACQT management team (Chalmers-led), overlapping institutionally with Johansson and the B004 work, and would recuse on B004 if it advanced.
Danielsson declares a research interest in dark energy that may bias him toward B016, which he has moved to an alternative.

Lindroth declares she is an atomic theorist who may overvalue B019, and notes a long collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, none of whom are on the shortlist.

Pearce (chair) reports no known link to Katori, Ye or any other shortlisted name, and that PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur work is unrelated to atomic clocks. He relies on colleagues for atomic, condensed-matter and quantum-information topics.
Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson report no specific conflict. Mehlig and Olsson note only that Chalmers and Gothenburg are neighbouring institutions.
questions_for_round2: Can B019 supporters say in one sentence what is discovered beyond better numbers, and can Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson say whether that answer is sufficient given the 1997, 2005, 2012 and 2018 prizes?

For B019, does the committee want to check the priority record for the first Sr lattice clock (Katori, JILA, SYRTE) and the status of Lemonde and Derevianko before the final ballot, or are Katori and Ye accepted as the pair?
Should the citation for B019 rest on the instrument and its 1e-18 physics, with the redefinition of the second left out of the citation and the rationale?

For B047, is the committee prepared to prize the discovery of correlated and superconducting phases and the flat-band prediction without a settled pairing mechanism, and if not, what resolution would it wait for?

For B047, can the committee justify naming Jarillo-Herrero alone on the experimental side, or does the Cao and Fatemi omission, together with Bistritzer as third name, change its view of the configuration?
For B012, would a citation limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect be accepted by members who raised the 2016 overlap, and how should the absence of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang be handled?

Do members who named B004 as an alternative (Johansson, Lindroth) accept that the 2025 prize and the credit questions about the transmon should keep it out of this year's configuration, and should Johansson and Kroll formally recuse on it if it advances?

Would any member who has not listed a different pair move to or away from B019 or B047 if outside expert evaluation were requested on lattice-clock priority or on the pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene?
summary.chair_observation: Five of eight members explicitly prefer B019, two prefer B047 and one prefers B012, and B047 appears most often as a second choice. B019 has the cleanest two-name allocation and the strongest maturity case, but its supporters disagree with Eriksson, Mehlig and the caveats in their own statements about whether it is a discovery or a measured advance, and Danielsson and Johansson moved to it after reading the other ballots. B047 and B012 share a credit gap that cannot be closed within three names. Round 2 should resolve the discovery-versus-refinement question for B019, the timing question for B047 and the citation scope for B012 before any ranking is attempted.
